items.title: Armand Hug Interview, 1965-09-13
items.q: This uncle started easing me in professionally because he gave me a lot of encouragement.

ctx.x: Would you remember how you spelled his name, Bordeaux, you said?

Yes, he was a very good friend of the families. And his name was Edward Bordeaux, which was a French name, and I think the name was B-O-R-D-E-A-U-X. When did you first start playing professionally? Well, now there's a little gap in between, Charlie, that when I hit around ten years old, well, I actually took about a year, I guess, of private lessons. And then when I hit this period of about ten and a half to eleven years old, I kind of got disinterested. And we moved away from the Bank Street area out into…
Was that more or less a ragtime bass you were using there, or was it?

items.title: Armand Hug Interview, 1960-07-14
items.q: But he really gave me a lot of encouragement and helped me a lot in showing me how to fake and play jazz tunes.

ctx.x: Now, the people in those previous generations, did they play what you'd call jams?

Well, when I first started playing Dick, I can remember back that I knew a few piano players that played piano. And it seemed as though to me they played the real old ragtime piano. There was a good friend of mine, his name was Edward Bordeaux. I happen to think of him today, since I was coming up to this interview. The last I heard of him, he went to Memphis, and he was living there. But he never did play anywhere professionally. But he used to play a real good ragtime piano. And I used to just look for him to…
How were you when you went to see Mrs. Asset?
